best_for: Writers and developers who want to edit Markdown with the formatting shown as they type, without a subscription or an account.
description:
MarkText is a Markdown editor started by the developer Jocs and built in the open with more than 200 contributors, paid for by community sponsors.

Type two pound signs and a space, and the line turns into a heading on the spot; bold, italics and links snap into shape the moment you close them. Lists, nested items and checkboxes build as you go. Paste rich text from a web page and it comes in as clean Markdown. You can draw flowcharts and charts with Mermaid, Vega and Vega-Lite, add footnotes that renumber themselves, and get syntax coloring in code blocks. It comes with 33 light and dark themes, and since each one is plain CSS, you can change one or write your own.

points.title: Preview while you type
points.text: MarkText renders Markdown in place as you write, so headings, tables and math look finished in the editor. It follows CommonMark and GitHub Flavored Markdown, with KaTeX math, front matter and emoji.

points.title: Free under MIT
points.text: The editor is open source under the MIT license, with no paid tier and no sign-in.

points.title: Export is HTML and PDF
points.text: The project lists HTML and PDF as its export formats. If you need Word files, plan on a separate converter.

points.title: Writing modes
points.text: Besides the live view there are Source Code, Typewriter and Focus modes, and you can paste images straight from the clipboard.

points.title: Mac builds are split by chip
points.text: The project ships separate Apple silicon and Intel downloads rather than a universal app, and its README asks for macOS 13 or later. Homebrew disabled its cask on 2026-09-01 because the app fails Apple's Gatekeeper check, so expect a security prompt on first launch.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is x64 only
points.text: The Flatpak listed here is a Flathub build for x64 that Flathub does not mark as verified. Arm Linux users have no Flatpak option here.

points.title: Windows has the history
points.text: Windows installers come for x64 and Arm64, per user or for all users. The Windows listing keeps 11 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
